newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Assembly proposes $2 bln school bond act.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Assembly proposes $2 bln school bond act.

text.p: New York Assembly proposed Wednesday a huge five-year education plan which includes a $2 billion bond act and aims to improve schools without forcing local districts to raise spending.

Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, estimated that the "School Facility Health and Safety Bond Act," if approved, would enable the state to finance as much as $6 billion of capital construction.
The plan would raise to 50 percent how much Albany reimbursed localities for bonds they issued for capital construction.
The new program, called the Learning, Achieving, Developing by Distributing Educational Resources plan or LADDER for short, also includes $250 million for minor school maintenance and repairs.

"Kids shouldn't learn math by counting the pieces of plaster or raindrops falling from the ceiling," the Speaker said, in prepared remarks. Some of New York State's schools, especially ones in New York City, have been blasted by education advocates because they are in poor condition.

Both Gov. George Pataki and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, have put forward ambitious plans to slash school property taxes, which have climbed as the state has cut aid, and become a source of conflict between the local governments and Albany. And the Republican governor has called for a constitutional amendment that would prevent the state from making localities pay for programs Albany did not fund.

Assemblyman Steven Sanders, D-Manhattan, who chairs the Assembly's Education Committee, in prepared remarks, said the new plan would restore the state's share of spending on education to 44 percent by 2001, the highest level since 1988. State aid has fallen to 37.8 percent under Pataki, he said, adding that under the LADDER plan it would rise by $979 million or 9.23 percent in fiscal 1998.
